name: camber-beam
title: Camber Beam
description: A full-width 1px top rule that is a load-bearing beam: flat and nearly invisible when healthy, bows downward at midspan as load metrics degrade, and fractures with a hairline gap plus a status row when the service is down.
useWhen: ambient service health that should cost zero layout while merely degraded and only claim a banner row on an actual outage — strain maps to a single geometric parameter (deflection of an otherwise plain border), not a weather-like field spread across the whole width (pressure-front) and not a narrated history of past phases (chronicle-bar); pick this specifically when the signal is 'is it fine right now', not 'how did we get here'.
instruction: A system-status banner built as an SVG beam sitting where a 1px top border would normally be: `M0,y Q(w/2),y+d w,y`, one quadratic path whose deflection `d` at midspan is the entire severity dial. `w` is the container's real measured pixel width (ResizeObserver, redrawn on resize) rather than a viewBox fraction, so downstream measurements like the fracture gap land as literal on-screen pixels regardless of how wide the banner is. Three tiers, driven by a `status` prop (healthy/degraded/down) plus a `severity` 0-1 prop that only matters while degraded: healthy holds d at 0, a dead-straight rule at --border, effectively invisible; degraded targets d = severity * 12px; down hides the single path and crossfades in two half-span paths, each anchored at its outer edge and drooping toward a literal 2px gap at the break, while a status text row height-animates open beneath via a grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr transition — the row claims real layout only in this state, so a degraded-but-working service stays peripheral and free. Every deflection change (a status/severity change while not down) is driven by an underdamped spring (k=130, zeta=0.32) integrated on a rAF loop and written directly to the path's `d` attribute (no React re-render per frame) — deliberately underdamped so the beam visibly overshoots and wobbles before settling, reading as a physical member responding to new load rather than an eased tween. Stroke color is a pure function of the spring's current value, color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) pct%, var(--border) (100-pct)%) where pct = d/12px clamped to 0-100 — it crossfades border toward foreground exactly in step with the wobble, never on its own separate timeline. Accessibility: the SVG is aria-hidden entirely; a visually hidden role=status aria-live=polite region mirrors only *tier crossings* in words ('Service degraded: response times elevated.' / 'Service down.' / a healthy recovery message) and never fires on a same-tier severity change, since narrating every metric tick would flood the live region; the fracture's status row is always a genuine visible paragraph, never geometry standing in for copy, so a fracture is legible without any assistive tech at all. A focusable button at the beam's right end (aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded, an accessible name) opens a small role=dialog metrics panel listing whatever label/value pairs are passed in; it toggles on click, but Escape closes it from anywhere in the document the instant it's open (not conditional on focus being inside it), so the control is always guaranteed closed before anything re-opens it by selector rather than depending on click parity, and a click outside the panel/button also closes it. Under prefers-reduced-motion (read live via a matchMedia change listener) the spring is skipped entirely — every deflection change jumps straight to its target value with no settle — and the group crossfades plus the status-row height transition both become instant swaps; the fracture's visible text and the live-region wording are completely unaffected either way. Pure DOM + SVG + CSS, no canvas, zero dependencies.
